results.name: Calf Raise From Deficit With Chair Supported
instructions: Stand on the edge of a raised platform or step, with your heels hanging off the edge, and hold onto a chair for support.
Position your feet hip-width apart, ensuring your toes are firmly on the platform.
Slowly raise your heels as high as possible, engaging your calf muscles and lifting your body.
Lower your heels back down past the edge of the platform to feel a stretch in your calves. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use the chair for balance but avoid leaning on it heavily to ensure your legs are doing the work.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure your heels drop below the platform to achieve a full range of motion and stretch.
results.description: Calf Raise From Deficit With Chair Supported is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

results.name: Calf Raise Leg Press Machine
instructions: Sit on the leg press machine and position your feet shoulder-width apart on the higher portion of the footplate with your toes pointing up.
Press the footplate by extending your legs and keeping a slight bend in your knees.
Push through your forefeet to raise the footplate as much as possible, squeezing your calf muscles.
Slowly lower your forefeet down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your legs slightly bent throughout the exercise to avoid placing stress on your knees.
Focus on a full range of motion, pushing your forefeet as much as possible for deep muscle activation.
Exhale as you raise your heels and inhale as you lower them back down.
results.description: Calf Raise Leg Press Machine is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.

results.name: Calf Raise With Wall Support
instructions: Stand facing a wall with your feet hip-width apart. Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height for support.
Position your feet flat on the floor, ensuring they are parallel to each other.
Slowly raise your heels as high as possible, lifting your body and engaging your calf muscles.
Lower your heels back to the floor in a controlled manner. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on lifting your heels fully and pausing briefly at the top of the movement to maximize muscle activation.
Use the wall for balance but ensure your legs are doing the work.
Keep your knees slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints.
results.description: Calf Raise With Wall Support is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

results.name: Calf Raise on Hack Squat Machine
instructions: Stand on the hack squat machine with your shoulders under the pads and your feet hips-width apart on the foot platform, with your toes pointing forward and your heels hanging off the edge.
Extend your legs to release the safety handles, keeping a slight bend in your knees.
Push through your forefeet to raise your heels as high as possible, squeezing your calf muscles at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your legs slightly bent throughout the exercise to avoid placing stress on your knees.
Focus on a full range of motion, lowering your heels as much as possible for a deep muscle activation.
Exhale as you raise your heels and inhale as you lower them back down.
results.description: Calf Raise on Hack Squat Machine is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.

results.name: Chair Back Lunge Left Resistance Band
instructions: Attach one end of a resistance band to a sturdy chair or similar support and the other end to your left ankle. Stand facing the chair with your right foot firmly planted on the floor.

Step back with your left foot, keeping your right foot in place, and lower your body into a lunge position by bending both knees, ensuring your right knee is directly above your right ankle and your left knee is hovering just above the floor.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
tips: Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on keeping your front knee aligned over your ankle to avoid putting excess strain on your knee joint.
Maintain balance by keeping your hands steady and holding the chair.
results.description: Chair Back Lunge Left Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Chair Bulgarian Split Squats Bodyweight Left
instructions: Stand a few feet in front of a chair, facing away from it. Place your left foot on the chair behind you, with the top of your foot resting on the seat.
Position your right foot firmly on the floor, a comfortable distance in front of the chair.
Lower your body by bending your right knee and hip, keeping your torso upright, until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee is close to the floor.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
tips: Keep your front knee aligned with your toes to avoid putting unnecessary strain on your knee.
Focus on driving through the heel of your front foot to engage your glutes and quadriceps effectively.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your back foot remains stable on the chair to maintain proper alignment.
results.description: Chair Bulgarian Split Squats Bodyweight Left is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Chair Elevated Single Leg Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your left heel placed on the edge of a chair, your right leg extended bent up towards the ceiling.
Position your arms by your sides with your palms facing down for stability.
Engage your core and glutes to lift your hips off the floor.
Hold the position briefly at the top, squeezing your glutes, then slowly lower your hips back to the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
tips: Ensure your heel remains firmly on the chair to provide a stable base for the movement.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Focus on squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement to enhance muscle engagement.
results.description: Chair Elevated Single Leg Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Lower Back.
